result.title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
result.summary: How many observations are needed to estimate a common rotation in two-dimensional overcomplete independent component analysis? We study equally spaced mixing columns with known source count, common source law, and column norm. For a fixed non-Gaussian fourth-order Gram-Charlier source law, the rotation is identifiable modulo the column spacing. Yet the sample size for fixed relative angular accuracy grows exponentially with the source count. We characterize this sample size, up to absolute constants, by the reciprocal of the squared Hellinger distance between two rotations separated by half the column spacing. An explicit radially weighted phase estimator attains this scale uniformly over the rotation family, using the observation radius to prevent cancellation in the mean of an angular harmonic. We also determine the exact exponential decay rate of single-observation total variation for the same pair. This gives bounds on the sample size exponent; its exact value remains open. Finally, a noisy binary-source example shows how an exact zero line of the observed characteristic function can have an exponentially small normal derivative.

AI.brief_summary: 研究二维过完备 ICA 中等间距混合列下共同旋转的可辨识性与估计代价，证明固定相对角精度所需样本量随源数指数增长，并用相邻旋转间的 Hellinger 距离刻画该规模，给出可达到该尺度的相位估计器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可辨识但难以估计」及以 Hellinger 距离量化潜变量结构区分难度的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态可辨识性、所需监督量与视觉证据筛选成本提供分析视角，可供核查其可迁移性。
